Description: Annual, succulent, salt-tolerant plant with fleshy green stems. Grows in coastal salt marshes and highly saline soils. Used as an edible vegetable and for oil production.
Soil moisture: Moist saline root environment, with periodic exposure; permanent deep flooding is not necessary.
Soil salinity: Highly salt-tolerant halophyte. Optimal experimental salt concentration approximately 15 g/L (257 mM NaCl).
Irrigation: Suitably managed saline or brackish water. Requires consistent water availability. Exact crop water requirement is not well established.

Description: Variable, trailing, softly hairy vine. Fruits vary in size, shape, rind and colour. A plant should be permitted to carry approximately four fruits.
Irrigation: Approximately 400–600 mm per growing season, supplied by rainfall and irrigation together.

Description: Small herb with a short central stem (crown), rosette of dark-green trifoliate leaves, runners and fleshy red fruits with seeds embedded in the surface. Runners develop during summer and are used for propagation. Fruits are rich in vitamin C and consumed fresh, frozen or processed.
Soil moisture: Soil moisture not specified; observe plant behaviour.
Soil salinity: Yield loss begins at approximately 0.7–1.0 dS/m.
Grow Months: Planting in October, with the main harvest campaign February–June.

Description: Small evergreen, thorny tree reaching up to 10 m. Large white flowers and globose fruits, often bright orange-red when ripe.
Irrigation: Regular irrigation adjusted to rainfall and soil moisture; approximately 90–120 cm per growing period.

Description: Vigorous, twining herbaceous legume with stems up to 4 m and a thickened or tuberous taproot. Dwarf forms exist. Red or white flowers, trifoliate leaves and flattened pods up to 40 cm long.

Variable, erect, more or less densely hairy herb with a large, cylindrical, thickened, fleshy root. Leaves can reach 60 cm. Root size varies considerably between cultivars. Edible portion consists of the thickened hypocotyl and upper taproot.
Soil moisture: Moist, well-drained soil; avoid waterlogging. Recommended soil-water tension: 5–30 kPa.
Soil salinity: Yield reduction begins above approximately 1.0 dS/m ECe.

Description: Variable, erect or spreading, coarsely hairy herbaceous plant, approximately 0.7–2 m tall. Many varieties produce red or yellow fruits of different sizes and shapes.
Soil moisture: Well-drained soil. Avoid waterlogging; medium-textured or organic soils are suitable.

Description: Perennial evergreen tree producing fleshy drupes containing a hard stone and an oil-rich seed. Cultivars vary considerably in fruit size, shape, oil content and flavour.
Soil moisture: Well-drained soil; waterlogging should be avoided.
Soil salinity: Tolerates mild saline conditions; exact threshold unspecified.
Irrigation: Traditionally rainfed, but supplementary irrigation is useful in low-rainfall areas. Particularly important during fruit development.

Description: A small tree, 3-6 m in height, with stout, stiff thorns. The fruits are 5-10 cm long, yellow and usually oval in shape.
Grow Months: October–April for winter lemon varieties and February–September for summer varieties.

Description: A deciduous perennial shrub, typically 2–3 m tall, with sweet blue-black berries.
